issue_context.title: [Feature] Allow to use wildcard in --project <name>
issue_context.body:
I have a `playwright.config.ts` in which I define 16 projects.

- 5x Tests running in Chrome in 5 different view port sizes
- 5x Tests running in Firefox in 5 different view port sizes
- 5x Tests running in Webkit in 5 different view port sizes
- 1x API test

Each test has a different name but follows a specific schema. Example:

- `ui-small-chrome`
- `ui-large-firefox`
- `api`

To run all tests, expect the `api` tests I need to use `npx playwright --project=ui-small-chrome --project=ui-large-firefox --project=...`.

What I would like to do is run `npx playwright --project=ui-*`.

I would expect this command to run all projects whose name start with `ui`.
comments:
Adding functionality to run projects based on a regex would also be helpful for CI contexts such as github actions, making it easier to run multiple projects at a time manually, rather than having to run them separately. E.g. running only mobile projects or desktop projects.

'npx playwright test --project mobile*'

review_comments: Why do we force full string match, rather than do a substring one?
In order to not break backwards compatibility.
Do we support this syntax in --grep?
Yes, its a copy of the normal `forceRegExp` and was adapted for the "whole string match" default.
nit: return false in the end? I'd also do `unmatchedProjectFilters.add(projectName);` there instead of deleting from the set.
Reversing unmatchedProjectFilters moves the same complexity to the end, keeping it for now.
